newsitem.title: USA: U.S. should avoid Helms-Burton clash -- Spain's Rato.
newsitem.headline: U.S. should avoid Helms-Burton clash -- Spain's Rato.

text.p: Spanish Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said on Monday the United States should avoid a clash with Europe over the Helms-Burton legislation against Cuba.
Rato said that Washington should use the six month hiatus in the U.S.-European Union dispute agreed in March to try to adapt its legislation to international standards.
"We should use the six month delay to avoid a confrontation," he said in a brief meeting with reporters on the fringes of the spring meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
The European Union challenged the validity of the Helms-Burton law last year, seeking a ruling from the World Trade Organization.
Both sides agreed to postpone their dispute until October to try to seek agreement.

The law, enacted in March 1996, included sanctions against foreigners who invested in assets siezed by Cuban communist president Fidel Castro after 1959. Spain is one of the largest investors in Cuba.
